text: You'll spend about six years of your life dreaming.
And scientists still can't fully explain why.
One idea: memory. While you sleep, your brain replays your day, and files away what matters.
Scientists have even watched rats replay their maze runs in their sleep.
Another idea: emotions. Dreaming may help your brain process feelings, like overnight therapy.
A third: practice. Some researchers think dreams are a threat simulator, rehearsing danger before it happens.
And a fourth says it's just noise: random brain signals that your mind turns into a story.
Meanwhile, your body is paralyzed, so you can't act it out.
Most dreams are gone within minutes of waking.
So, do you remember your last one?
